title: Apricot sauce
desc: Dried apricots simmered soft in water with a little brown sugar and cider vinegar, mashed to a thick, spoonable sauce and finished with butter. Sweet, mellow and golden, with just enough acid to cut rich meat. It goes with roast pork, turkey and ham, and it tastes like apricot preserves made for the dinner plate.

title: Cranberry and shallot agrodolce
desc: Shallots cooked slowly in olive oil until soft and golden, then simmered with fresh cranberries, brown sugar, red wine vinegar, orange and a sprig of rosemary. The Italian sweet-sour method gives a savory cranberry relish for rich meat: sweet first, then a clean sour edge, with no mustard and no chile heat.

title: Cranberry-orange sauce
desc: The familiar whole-berry cranberry sauce, made in two stages. Two thirds of the berries cook until they burst and release their pectin, which sets the sauce. The last third goes in at the end and stays whole. Orange zest, fresh juice and a pinch of salt keep it bright rather than only sweet.

title: Cumin-roasted carrots with salsa verde
desc: Carrots hard-roasted at 220 °C with toasted cumin until their edges caramelize, then dressed while warm in a salsa verde of parsley, mint, capers, anchovy, garlic and lemon. The savory version of a holiday carrot side: the carrots bring their own sweetness, and the herbs, salt and acid cut through rich mains and creamy sides.

ingredients.item: carrots, rainbow or orange, medium thickness
flat-leaf parsley, leaves and tender stems
extra-virgin olive oil, for the salsa verde

title: Garlic and thyme roasted carrots
desc: Carrots hard-roasted at 220 °C with fresh thyme until their edges caramelize, then tossed hot in a gently cooked garlic oil and finished with lemon and parsley. Familiar, savory flavors. A little white miso in the garlic oil gives depth without tasting of miso.

ingredients.item: carrots, rainbow or orange, medium thickness
extra-virgin olive oil, for the garlic oil

title: Jalapeño cheddar skillet cornbread
desc: Buttermilk cornbread baked in a preheated cast iron skillet, so the bottom and edges fry crisp in brown butter. The cornmeal soaks in the buttermilk first for a tender crumb. Sharp cheddar, seeded jalapeño and corn kernels run through it, and honey keeps it lightly sweet.

title: Smoked pork shoulder
desc: Pulled smoked pork shoulder finished with a cider vinegar sauce, in two versions. Buy it from a barbecue restaurant and reheat it with stock and the sauce, or dry-brine a bone-in Boston butt, smoke it at 121 °C until a probe slides in, rest it and pull it.

ingredients.item: kosher salt, for the dry brine
light brown sugar, for the rub
hickory, oak or apple wood chunks

title: Strawberry tres leches cake
desc: A separated-egg sponge soaked overnight in evaporated, condensed and whole milk, spread with a thick strawberry compote and topped with crème fraîche whipped cream colored and flavored with freeze-dried strawberry powder. Built for strawberries out of season: frozen berries cooked down and freeze-dried berries carry far more flavor than winter fresh ones.

title: Braised beef chuck with mushrooms and thyme
desc: A boneless chuck roast cut into large pieces, dry-brined, seared hard, and braised low in porter and stock with onions, garlic, tomato paste and thyme until it yields to a spoon. Browned cremini go in at the end and a splash of vinegar sharpens the sauce. Built to be cooked a day ahead and reheated on the stovetop.

title: Cider-glazed baby back ribs
desc: Two racks of baby back ribs, dry-brined overnight, rubbed with brown sugar, smoked paprika, mustard, fennel and sage, cooked low until a probe slides between the bones, then lacquered with a reduced apple cider and mustard glaze. Smoke them on any smoker, or slow-bake them the day before and glaze them in a hot oven, or do one rack each way.

title: Cranberry mostarda
desc: Fresh cranberries cooked into a loose syrup with brown sugar, red wine vinegar, shallot, orange and whole mustard seeds, then finished off the heat with cold-bloomed mustard powder. Sweet, sharply sour and nose-clearing, it is a cranberry sauce built for rich meats.

title: Turkey and sage meatballs with brown butter gravy
desc: Ground turkey bound with a sourdough-and-milk panade and a bloomed sheet of gelatin, so the lean meat stays juicy after roasting and a day in the fridge. The meatballs roast hard at 230 °C for browning, then sit overnight in a brown butter and sage pan gravy built on the sheet-pan drippings, soy and cider vinegar.

ingredients.item: neutral oil (refined avocado, rice bran, or grapeseed)

title: Apple crumble with brown butter oat topping
desc: A 9 x 13 inch crumble built on a two-apple blend: Granny Smith for acid and structure, Honeycrisp or Pink Lady for aromatic sweetness, set with a small dose of cornstarch so the juices bake into a glossy syrup instead of a puddle. The topping is brown butter worked into flour, oats, brown sugar, and toasted pecans, then chilled so it bakes into crisp clusters rather than a sandy sheet.

ingredients.item: Honeycrisp, Pink Lady, or Braeburn apples
freshly grated nutmeg or ground cardamom

title: Arugula, pear, and pomegranate salad with goat cheese
desc: Baby arugula, paper-thin pear, pomegranate arils, salted toasted almonds, and crumbled fresh goat cheese, dressed at the table with a shallot, cider, and dijon vinaigrette that carries a spoonful of white miso. Built as the sharp, raw, crisp counterweight to a rich holiday table: pepper from the arugula, acid from the cider and pomegranate, crunch from the almonds, and lactic tang from the cheese.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, for the almonds
pears, ripe but firm (Bosc or Bartlett)

title: Beef Wellington with red wine jus
desc: Center-cut beef tenderloin, dry-brined and seared, wrapped in prosciutto and a dry mushroom duxelles, then in all-butter puff pastry, and baked hot on a preheated sheet until the pastry is deep gold and the beef is medium-rare to the edge. Two days of short, separate steps make the hardest roast in the repertoire manageable, and a reduced red wine jus supplies the acid the pastry and beef need.

ingredients.item: center-cut beef tenderloin, trimmed and tied
neutral oil (refined avocado, rice bran, or grapeseed)

title: Crème fraîche
desc: Heavy cream cultured at room temperature with a spoonful of live buttermilk until lactic acid bacteria sour and thicken it. Two ingredients and two days of waiting give a cream that is nutty, gently sour and thick enough to hold a spoon upright, and that does not curdle in a hot sauce.

title: Hasselback potato gratin
desc: Unrinsed Yukon Gold slices tossed in garlic-and-thyme-infused cream with gruyère and parmigiano, then stood upright in tight rows so the exposed edges roast into a crisp, frilled top while the buried half braises creamy. The format splits the gratin into two textures in one dish: a crackling ridge of browned potato and cheese above a soft, starch-thickened base.

title: Herb-crusted rack of lamb with cranberry mostarda
desc: Two frenched racks of lamb dry-brined overnight, seared fat-side down in cast iron, brushed with dijon, pressed into a crust of breadcrumbs, parsley, rosemary, thyme, garlic, lemon zest, and parmigiano, then roasted at 220 °C to a 52 °C pull and rested to medium-rare. A sharp cranberry mostarda (cranberries, vinegar, two mustard seeds, and cold-bloomed dry mustard) does the job that cranberry sauce does for turkey: it is the acid and the heat that cut the lamb fat.

ingredients.item: neutral oil (refined avocado, rice bran, or grapeseed)

title: Maple-cumin roasted carrots
desc: Carrots hard-roasted at 220 °C until their edges caramelize, then lacquered in the last minutes with a glaze of maple syrup, white miso, freshly toasted cumin, and Aleppo pepper, and finished with lemon, toasted pistachios, dill, and mint. Sweet, savory, warm-spiced, and bright, and built to sit at room temperature so the oven is free for the mains.

ingredients.item: carrots, rainbow or orange, medium thickness
maple syrup, dark and robust grade
extra-virgin olive oil, for the glaze
shelled pistachios, toasted and roughly chopped

title: Thunder tea rice (lei cha)
desc: The Hakka one-bowl meal: a dark green soup of green tea, Thai basil, mint, laksa leaf, cilantro, toasted sesame and peanuts, pounded to a paste and loosened with hot water, poured over jasmine rice crowned with separately stir-fried long beans, choy sum, golden tofu, sweet-salty preserved radish and roasted peanuts. Bitter, herbal and nutty in the soup; salty, sweet and crunchy on the rice.

title: Chocolate stout cake
desc: A small two-layer 4-inch chocolate cake where dry Irish stout replaces the liquid, melted with butter and blooming the cocoa so its roasted-barley bitterness reads as deeper chocolate. Sour cream and dark brown sugar keep the crumb dense and damp, and a lightly sweetened whipped cream-cheese frosting sits on top like the head on a pint.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, plus a little for the pans
full-fat block cream cheese, room temp

title: Chocolate Texas sheet cake
desc: A thin, fudgy half-sheet chocolate cake built from a boiled butter-coffee-cocoa base and buttermilk, then flooded while still warm with a poured brown-butter cocoa icing and toasted pecans. The warm-on-warm pour is the defining move: the icing sinks a few millimeters into the crumb and sets into a soft fudge layer rather than sitting on top as frosting.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, plus a little for the pan

title: Gari (sushi pickled ginger)
desc: Young ginger shaved paper-thin, salted, and blanched for a few seconds to tame its heat, then packed into a warm sweet rice-vinegar brine. After a day it is crisp, sweet-sharp, and naturally blush pink. It is the palate reset between pieces of sushi, so it needs to be clean and bright, not candied.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt (for the salt draw)

title: Sushi rice (sumeshi)
desc: Japanese short-grain rice washed clear, cold-soaked with kombu, cooked slightly drier than table rice, then cut through with a warm vinegar-sugar-salt seasoning (awasezu) and fanned to body temperature. The result is glossy, separate-but-cohesive grains with a clean sweet-sour-saline edge that holds up against raw fish, nori, and soy.
